transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Jai Patel (ACME CTO), Maya Chen (ML Engineer), Omar Ruiz (Infra), Priya Shah (Product)
---
00:00 Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna focus on scoping the POC this afternoon, quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, timeline.
00:18 Jai (ACME CTO): sounds good, Lena. quick note: we're evaluating a few vendors, but main goals are predictability and cost for our high-volume summarization API.
00:25 Marco (Redwood SE): great, thanks. can you run through current traffic and payload shapes? rough qps, concurrency, token counts, that kinda stuff.
00:34 Maya (ML Eng): sure. baseline: average steady-state QPS is ~30 reqs/sec, our peaks hit 110-130 qps during batch crunch windows. concurrency currently around 70 active connections during peaks but typical conversational concurrency is 25-40.
00:53 Marco (SE): ok that helps. what's the token distribution? input vs output?
00:58 Maya: inputs average 120 tokens (most are user messages + context), outputs vary — typical summary outputs are 250-400 tokens, 95th percentile around 650. about 40% of requests are shorter (under 60 tokens output) and 10% are long ( > 800 tokens) but those are rare.
01:21 Lena: so to restate, steady qps 25-35, peak 110-130, concurrency 25-70, avg in 120, avg out ~300, p95 out ~650. is that accurate?
01:30 Maya: yep that's the ballpark.
01:33 Jai: our success criteria for POC: prove we can hit 95th percentile latency under 1s for short outputs and under 2.5s for mid outputs at our peak profile, maintain quality parity with our current model, and show predictable unit cost within 15% of our target.
01:50 Marco: good, that's actionable. for latency SLOs we need to clarify whether those are end-to-end including network, or server-side only.
01:58 Jai: end-to-end as experienced by our API. so network and auth add-ons included.
02:03 Marco: noted. for benchmark planning Redwood will run two modes: hosted endpoint simulating your traffic, and a dedicated reserved run to show deterministic throughput. we'll provide a harness that replays the 5k sample with timing distribution you provide.
02:18 Omar (Infra): on network, for the private pilot we'll need VPC peering and SSO. what are typical requirements?
02:25 Lena: for private deployments we support VPC peering and customer-managed subnets. Marco will include a network checklist. we also provide SOC2 docs and can integrate with your KMS for key management.
02:36 Marco: quick perf modeling note — because a lot of your traffic is conversational with repeated prefixes, KV/prefix caching can reduce compute by~25-40% for follow-ups, depending on cache hit rate. How many requests are follow-ups vs new sessions?
02:49 Maya: around 55% are continued sessions where prefix context is re-used.
02:53 Marco: ok that increases effective throughput and lowers cost. we'll model both with and without prefix caching.
02:57 Lena: can I ask about your tolerance for caching-related staleness? some customers are fine with eventual consistency for cached tokens, others need strict fresh context.
03:06 Jai: we need fresh context for security-sensitive items, but for summarization many follow-ups can use cached prefixes. we'll flag sensitive flows.
03:13 Marco: perfect. on model variants: are you looking to use an open model or a tuned private checkpoint?
03:20 Maya: we prefer an open base model initially; we might finetune later. latency/cost wins from quantized variants are attractive but we need to validate quality.
03:31 Lena: as part of the POC we'll run the open model in both FP16 and int8-ish quantized variants and report quality metrics vs tokens and latency.
03:40 Marco: benchmark metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens, and quality regression on provided eval prompts. we'll also surface per-token breakdown and batch sizes used.
03:55 Priya (Product): timeline question — how long for an end-to-end pilot?
03:59 Lena: typical POC is 2-4 weeks for benching and validation, then a pilot (private/dedicated) for another 4-8 weeks depending on infra readiness. so production in ~8-12 weeks if all goes smoothly.
04:12 Jai: ok reasonable. who owns bench runs? Redwood or ACME?
04:16 Marco: Redwood will run an initial hosted benchmark using your sample dataset; if you want dedicated results we can schedule a reserved run where ACME provides network access or we deploy private nodes.
04:27 Omar: on the reserved run, we need a network plan and IP allowlist. we'll coordinate with Marco.
04:33 Marco: noted. for the benchmark we'll need: the 5k sample records, a token histogram CSV, a target QPS schedule (steady + peak windows), and any eval prompts.
04:43 Maya: we'll produce that. question on concurrency: you said concurrency matters more than raw qps for tail latency, any guidance on shaping traffic?
04:51 Marco: yes tail latency is sensitive to concurrency and batch scheduling. we'll show tradeoffs: lower p95 by reducing concurrency or using more dedicated capacity. there's also batching parameters we can tune; Redwood Optimize will recommend batching/quantization profiles.
05:06 Lena: pricing note — for hosted pilots we do usage pricing; for Dedicated we can offer a reserved monthly commit. I'll send both price scenarios and an initial SOW.
05:15 Jai: good. also security: we need SOC2 report, SAML SSO, audit logs and KMS support.
05:22 Lena: we have SOC2 and KMS integrations; Marco will attach security docs. SSO is supported with SAML.
05:27 Marco: one more techn detail: if you have multi-tenant datasets, we can route by policy and use per-route isolated models. We'll include routing policies in the config example.
05:38 Maya: perf question — can you model 130 qps peak with p95 <2s for the heavy output (300-600 tokens)?
05:45 Marco: yes with Dedicated capacity and tuned batching we can approach that; exact numbers depend on model choice and GPU type. we'll run a baseline on the same model you intend to use and report.
05:55 Speaker 1 (auto-transcription artefact): um hmm 
05:58 Lena: haha thanks speaker 1. ok next steps recap: Redwood sends benchmark template and pricing/SOW, ACME provides 5k samples + histograms, schedule live benchmark.
06:12 Jai: timeline: we'll aim to get samples by 06/22, expect the hosted bench the week after, and a decision on Dedicated by early July.
06:21 Lena: perfect. any final questions?
06:24 Omar: just to confirm, network access for private pilot will require our security team sign-off; we'll aim to have that by 06/24.
06:31 Maya: and I'll prepare the eval prompts too.
06:34 Lena: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with an email and the attachments.
06:40 Transcript notes: some speaker labels may be generic; minor transcription errors present (product names, acronyms). references: benchmark template (link to redwood bench doc), SSO/SOC2 pack (link), pricing SOW (to be shared).
---
End of transcript
